richText.text: Remember to give it a thumbs up and favorite if it helped you, I need that stuff for self validation :)

Use them. That's it... this section's only purpose is the first -and last- friendly reminder that this game loves you and is giving you enough save slots for an entire household to play it multiple teams each, so the least you can do is use them. Also, do try to prioritize the missables over anything else, this will save you headaches having to reload any of the aforementioned backups.
They are all marked with a ⚠ to at the beginning of the entry to keep things simple.
I recommend the Standard Sphere Grid but the choice is ultimately yours. You should be able to beat everything with either one regardless of difficulty.
860 nodes, with 85 unremovable nodes and 775 manipulable nodes. Allows you to have overall superior stats during the endgame but everyone follows their intended job path for the main story.

805 nodes with 85 unremovable nodes and 720 manipulable nodes. Allows you to quickly customize your characters to your exact needs during the main story since everyone shares starting point and there are less obstructions in the Grid, but there are also less nodes to customize during the endgame.

This game has built-in cheats that can be accessed by pressing ESC on the keyboard. I only mention this since controller players may never find them and have no way of using them naturally unless installing the Untitled Project X mod.
Extra: Head Northwest in the \[Submerged Ruins\] to use the Al Bhed Compilation Sphere if you have collected the Primers during another playthrough and would like to import them to this one.

sessions.title: POINT OF NO RETURN: Inside Sin

richText.text: ⚠ DO NOT PICK "SIN" AT THE AIRSHIP IF YOU PLAN TO RECRUIT DURREN FOR BLITZBALL.
Durren can be found outside of \[Cavern of the Stolen Fayth\] near the Rusty Sword if you want him to warm up your bench.

Last Warning The Save Sphere at \[Sin - Tower of the Dead\] is as far as you can make it. I'd suggest to make a secondary save here, go beat the game normally and then have fun with the endgame, otherwise any semblance of difficulty will go out of the window permanently.
Go grind at the Monster Arena if any of the areas below are too strong. Passwords
Coordinates
⚠ Item (Various): You can get a weapon with No Encounter from Geosgaeno at a 50% drop rate.
Item (Onion Knight): Loot from a treasure chest at X.

Aeon (Anima): To enter the Chamber of the Fayth you need to have used all Destruction Spheres at every Cloister of Trials (this includes Zanarkand which you need to backtrack for) and looted their respective chests.
⚠ Item (Various): There's a "secret" minigame which requires to open all treasure chests across all four groups, but they may randomly contain a Mimic causing you to fail.

As far as I know there is no trick to circumvent the 1/240 odds you will be fighting against, so make sure to make a separate save if you intend to participate, otherwise the rewards will be permanently lost if you fail.
Al Bhed Primer (vol. XXVI): Starting at the Save Sphere turn left, then right at the next fork in the road until you reach a room with four chests in a big circle, the primer is right behind them.

Before we get anything started you need to buy Capture weapons for at least your main party. I highly suggest you give Stonestrike to all of them so it carries you through 90% of the monsters, even the ones you are not strong enough to be capturing otherwise without some early grind. Gear Prep As we advance make our way through the Arena we want to start buying and customizing the Tetra armor pieces for all our party members. These are bought from Wantz near the entrance of \[Macalania Woods - South\] for 100,000 Gil each. Auto-Haste is no negotiable, other than that it's really your choice for the other three slots.
Note

: You could get the weapons too if you feel under-prepared, but the Arena will open up the grind for max stats so it's not that important, especially since the Celestial Weapons will make them obsolete "soon" enough. Not to mention the initial portion of the Arena requires to use weapons with Capture so... Max Stats Now that we completed the tutorial grind we can get started on the real grind!
Standard Grid: You can max basically all stats, minus two if you go for Break HP Limit.
Expert Grid: You need to min-max, Luck is the best stat in the game.

By far the most annoying grind in the entire game in my opinion, also the most useless one. So, Overdrive Modes are unlocked after fulfilling their conditions a number of times per each party member while fighting outside of the Monster Arena cause **** you. For example: Yuna learns the Healer Mode faster than anyone else by healing allies, while Auron learns Coward Mode slower than anyone else by fleeing from combat. I will not bother listing the number of times, but do know that most modes expect around a hundred, with the longest grind being Auron's Coward which needs a nice 1,000 repetitions.
Stoic: Character takes damage.
Warrior: Character damages an enemy.
Comrade: Allies take damage.
Healer: Character heals allies.
Tactician: Status attack succeeds.
Victim: Character hit with status attack.
Dancer: Character evades attack.
Avenger: Allies are KO'd.
Slayer: Character defeats an enemy.
Hero: Character defeats powerful enemy.
Rook: Character magically blocks an attack.
Victor: Party wins a battle.
Coward: Character flees from battle.
Ally: Character's turn.
Sufferer: Character suffers status ailments.
Daredevil: Character fights with low HP.
Loner: Character fights alone.

She only gets -and needs- Mix. Here are some great recipes:
Final Phoenix: Phoenix Down + Shining Gem.
Full HP recovery while also reviving dead allies to full.
Final Elixir: Hi-Potion + Lv.1 Key Sphere.
Full HP and MP recovery while also reviving dead allies to full.
Ultra NulAll: Healing Spring + Healing Spring.
Cheer, Focus, Aim, Reflex, NulBlaze, NulShock, NulTide, and NulFrost on all allies.
Hyper Mighty G: Healing Spring + Gambler's Spirit.
Shell, Protect, Haste, Regen, and Auto-Life on all allies.
Trio of 9999: Gambler's Spirit + Gambler's Spirit.
All allies deal at least 9,999 on every action. Great for the early end-game.
Use Spiral Cut 10 times, then Slice & Dice 30 times and finally Energy Rain 80 times.
